extracted.intended_audience: novelists and authors (including unagented authors) preparing unsolicited manuscript submissions to Tor/Forge
extracted.subtask_short: submitting a novel manuscript to Tor/Forge
extracted.subtask_description: Practical submission guidelines and requirements for authors (including those without agents) who want to submit a novel or other book-length work to the Tor/Forge imprint. Covers required packet contents, formatting/length guidance for excerpts and synopses, procedural rules (how and when to send), and pre-submission readiness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of unsolicited submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The are open to unsolicited submissions from authors without an agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit directly (no agent required). Note competition is fierce — they consider tens of thousands of projects every year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission medium: postal mail only
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should be made through the mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit electronically; follow the publisher's postal submission process exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No response to queries
rubrics_metrics.description: They do not respond to queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect query responses; do not send query emails or expect personalized acknowledgements beyond their stated procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required excerpt: first three chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission packets must include the first three chapters of your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This excerpt should be between 40-60 pages. Provide a clean, representative opening—the publisher specifically requests this portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a dated cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission packet must also include a dated cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter should be dated; presumably concise and professional, following the publisher's full guidelines (link provided on their site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a self-addressed stamped envelope (SASE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission packet must also include a self addressed and stamped envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASE is required for any mailed submission where you expect a reply; include correct postage and address formatting per guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a full synopsis with all important plot elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission packet must also include a synopsis of the entire book that includes all important plot elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete synopsis (not just a teaser) that reveals major plot points and resolution so editors can assess the full story.

rubrics_metrics.name: For series work, propose the first book only
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have written or plan to write a whole series, only propose the first book, not the series as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit series bibles or multiple-book proposals; focus the submission on the initial installment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the publisher's complete submission guidelines first
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you read their complete submission guidelines before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the publisher's full guidelines (link noted on the page) for details such as editor names, genre routing, formatting, and any updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert the correct editor for other genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Tom Doherty Associates also considers books in other genres as long as you follow the same guidelines and alert the correct editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting outside SF/F (e.g., women's literature, children's books), follow the same packet requirements and identify the appropriate editor on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no reply after six months, resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to note that if you do not receive a reply after six months, please resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow six months for consideration; if you haven't heard, send the packet again rather than assuming permanent rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each proposal will be reviewed by at least one editorial staff member
rubrics_metrics.description: Every proposal is reviewed by at least one member of the editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While competition is high, submitted packets are given at least one staff review — this is informational about process/expectation, not a guarantee of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher may close/open specific submission types (e.g., novellas)
rubrics_metrics.description: September 30th 2020: They are closed to general submissions due to COVID-19, but plan to reopen. Also they’ve held novella submissions during this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission windows and what formats are accepted (novellas, etc.) may change; check current status on the publisher site before preparing/submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission readiness: revise multiple times
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you revised your manuscript at least 3 times?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site requires authors to confirm they've revised their manuscript multiple times before proceeding; thorough revision improves professionalism and readiness for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission readiness: beta reader feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you gotten beta reader feedback?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked whether they've sought beta reader feedback—external readers can catch problems and improve the manuscript prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to study publisher's guidelines and catalog before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: I agree to only submit after carefully studying the publisher's guidelines and catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should confirm they will only submit after reviewing what the publisher publishes and their submission rules to avoid inappropriate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid submitting unpolished or inappropriate work
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting to un-polished or innapropriate work can ruin your reptuation and can (and has) cause a publisher to close submissions to everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit manuscripts that are not professionally revised or that don't fit the publisher's list; such submissions harm your reputation and may have broader negative effects.
